add-096.title: Fluffy Potato Ojja with Vegetables
add-096.culturalNotes: Baking powder is the secret of a fluffy, light ojja, and the mashed potato keeps it soft and firm so it doesn't break when flipped.

add-096-i3.name: Green and red bell pepper, small dice

add-096-i9.name: Salt, black pepper, cumin, ground coriander and a pinch of chilli

instructions.1: Whisk the eggs with the spices, then add the flour and baking powder and whisk until no lumps remain.
instructions.2: Add the mashed potato, onion, peppers and parsley and mix until even.
instructions.3: Heat the ghee and oil in a non-stick pan, pour in the mixture and level it, then cover on low heat for 8-10 minutes until the base sets and browns.
instructions.4: Flip the ojja onto a plate and slide it back into the pan on the other side for 5 minutes until cooked.
instructions.5: You can pour the mixture into a greased tray and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes, or fry spoonfuls as small patties.
instructions.6: Cut into wedges and serve with tahini or green salad.

add-097.title: Homemade Pomegranate Molasses
add-097.culturalNotes: Pomegranate molasses is essential in Levantine cooking for salads, muhammara and sfiha. Sour or sweet-sour pomegranates give the best balance.

instructions.1: Seed the pomegranates, pulse the seeds briefly in a blender and strain through a fine sieve.
instructions.2: Mix the juice, sugar and lemon in a wide pot over medium heat until boiling.
instructions.3: Lower the heat and simmer uncovered for 1-1½ hours, stirring occasionally, until reduced to a quarter and syrupy.
instructions.4: Let cool completely (it thickens as it cools), bottle and refrigerate.

add-098.title: Fresh Orange Juice (with Optional Carrot)
add-098.culturalNotes: Drink orange juice as soon as it is squeezed, as it loses vitamins and turns bitter with time. Local juicing oranges give more juice than navels.

add-098-i3.name: Boiled carrot (optional, for a thicker juice)

instructions.1: Wash the oranges, halve and squeeze with a juicer, or peel and blend then strain.
instructions.2: For the carrot version: blend the boiled carrot with a cup of the juice until smooth, then add to the rest.
instructions.3: Sweeten to taste and serve at once over ice.

add-099.title: Palestinian Musakhan Rolls
add-099.culturalNotes: Musakhan is a Palestinian dish traditionally served on taboon bread with a whole chicken. The rolls are a modern way to serve it as a starter; sumac and olive oil are its soul.

add-099-i5.name: Salt, black pepper and a pinch of cumin

add-099-i6.name: Saj or shrak bread, cut into triangles

instructions.1: Cook the onion in the olive oil over low heat for 15-20 minutes until completely soft and sweet without burning.
instructions.2: Add the sumac and spices, then the shredded chicken, and stir 5 minutes to absorb the flavour; add the pine nuts.
instructions.3: Put a little filling on the edge of each bread triangle, fold in the sides and roll tightly.
instructions.4: Arrange in a tray, brush with the olive oil left from the onion and bake at 200°C for 10-12 minutes until crisp.
instructions.5: Serve hot with yogurt or pomegranate molasses.

add-100.title: Tuna Salad with Corn
add-100.culturalNotes: Lemon and mustard soften the strong tuna smell. For a light version, replace all the mayonnaise with yogurt.

instructions.1: Drain the tuna well of oil or water and flake with a fork.
instructions.2: Add the corn, pepper, onion, parsley and pickles.
instructions.3: Mix the mayonnaise with the mustard, lemon and pepper and fold into the salad.
instructions.4: Chill 15 minutes and serve on toast, in lettuce leaves or as a sandwich filling.

add-101.title: Eggplant Fatteh with Yogurt
add-101.culturalNotes: Salting the eggplant before frying greatly reduces the oil it absorbs. Tahini in the yogurt stops it splitting and gives it a velvety texture.

add-101-i2.name: Arabic bread, cubed, toasted or fried

add-101-i3.name: Minced meat sautéed with onion and spices (optional)

add-101-i7.name: Lemon juice and salt
add-101-i7.standardAmount: juice of ½ lemon + a pinch

add-101-i9.name: Ghee and pine nuts or almonds to garnish

instructions.1: Sprinkle the eggplant cubes with salt and leave in a colander 20 minutes to release their water, then dry.
instructions.2: Fry the eggplant until golden, or brush with oil and roast in the oven, and drain on kitchen paper.
instructions.3: Whisk the yogurt with the tahini, garlic, lemon and salt until smooth.
instructions.4: Spread the bread in a serving dish, then the eggplant, then the minced meat if using, then cover with the yogurt sauce.
instructions.5: Toast the pine nuts in the ghee and pour sizzling over the yogurt, garnish with pomegranate and parsley and serve at once.

add-102.title: Homemade Greek Yogurt
add-102.culturalNotes: Greek yogurt is simply regular yogurt strained of its whey, so it is higher in protein and thicker. The longer it strains, the closer it gets to labneh.

instructions.1: Heat the milk until almost boiling, then let it cool until lukewarm (about 43°C).
instructions.2: Mix the starter with a little of the warm milk, then return it to the rest of the milk and stir.
instructions.3: Cover the container and wrap it in a blanket or place in a switched-off warm oven for 8 hours without moving it until set.
instructions.4: Pour the yogurt into a cheesecloth-lined sieve over a bowl and leave in the fridge 3-4 hours until the whey drains and it is very thick.
instructions.5: Stir until smooth and keep in an airtight container in the fridge for a week.

add-103.title: Pepperoni Pizza
add-103.culturalNotes: Putting the pepperoni on top of the cheese rather than under it lets the edges crisp and curl into little cups, with their spiced fat running into the cheese.

instructions.1: Knead the dough ingredients until smooth and elastic and leave an hour until doubled.
instructions.2: Roll the dough thin in a greased tray, leaving a slightly thicker edge.
instructions.3: Spread with the sauce and sprinkle with oregano, then the cheese, then lay the pepperoni slices on top.
instructions.4: Bake at the highest heat (240-250°C) for 12-15 minutes until the edges brown and the pepperoni edges crisp.
instructions.5: Leave 2 minutes before slicing so the cheese sets.

add-104.title: Basil Pesto
add-104.culturalNotes: Pesto comes from Genoa in Italy. A layer of oil on top and a little lemon keep it green. Toss with hot pasta and two spoonfuls of its cooking water.

instructions.1: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan for 2 minutes until lightly coloured and let cool.
instructions.2: Put the basil, cheese, pine nuts and garlic in a food processor and chop until combined.
instructions.3: Add the olive oil gradually with the processor running until smooth and creamy.
instructions.4: Adjust the salt and pepper, add the lemon, and store in a jar covered with a layer of oil in the fridge for a week.

add-105.title: French Onion Soup
add-105.culturalNotes: Slowly caramelising the onions is the whole secret of this French soup; rushing it on high heat burns them and makes them bitter instead of sweet.

instructions.1: Melt the butter with the oil, add the onions and stir until soft, then add the sugar and salt.
instructions.2: Cook the onions on low heat for 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until caramelised to a deep golden brown.
instructions.3: Sprinkle in the flour and stir a minute, then add the stock, thyme and bay leaf and simmer 20 minutes.
instructions.4: Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls, top each with a slice of bread and then the cheese.
instructions.5: Grill until the cheese melts and browns, and serve at once.

add-106.title: Pineapple Coconut Smoothie
add-106.culturalNotes: A tropical smoothie close to a piña colada without alcohol. Frozen pineapple gives it a thick, icy texture.

instructions.1: Put the coconut milk and yogurt in the blender first, then the pineapple, banana, honey and ice.
instructions.2: Blend until completely smooth, pour into two glasses and garnish with a pineapple slice or a sprinkle of coconut.

add-107.title: Egyptian Liver and Orzo Tagine
add-107.culturalNotes: This tagine is a favourite of Egypt's liver shops. Searing the liver quickly on very high heat keeps it tender, and it finishes cooking in the oven.

add-107-i10.name: Cumin, black pepper and chilli
add-107-i10.standardAmount: 1 tsp cumin + ½ pepper + a pinch of chilli

instructions.1: Toast the orzo in the ghee until golden, then add the stock and salt and cook until half the liquid is absorbed.
instructions.2: Sear the liver in the oil on very high heat for just 2 minutes until it changes colour, then remove.
instructions.3: Sauté the onion, then the garlic and peppers, add the tomato paste, tomato juice and spices and cook 5 minutes.
instructions.4: Mix the half-cooked orzo with the liver and sauce in a clay tagine.
instructions.5: Bake at 200°C for 20-25 minutes until the orzo absorbs the sauce and the top browns.
instructions.6: Squeeze over the lemon and serve hot in the tagine.

add-108.title: Jalapeño Cheddar Bites
add-108.culturalNotes: The double breadcrumb coating and freezing before frying stop the cheese leaking into the oil.

instructions.1: Mix the cheddar, cream cheese, jalapeño and spices until the mixture holds together.
instructions.2: Shape into walnut-sized balls, set on a tray and freeze 20 minutes.
instructions.3: Coat in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs, then egg and breadcrumbs again for a double layer.
instructions.4: Return to the freezer for 10 minutes to set the crust.
instructions.5: Fry in hot oil at 180°C for 2 minutes until golden and drain.
instructions.6: Serve at once with ranch or sweet chilli sauce.

add-109.title: Harissa Stuffed with Ashta and Walnuts
add-109.culturalNotes: Tahini on the base of the tray is a Levantine tradition that gives the harissa a crisp golden bottom and a subtle distinctive flavour.

add-109-i12.name: Syrup: sugar, water, lemon and orange-blossom water
add-109-i12.standardAmount: 2 cups sugar + 1½ cups water + a squeeze of lemon + 1 tbsp orange-blossom water

instructions.1: Boil the sugar, water and lemon for 10 minutes, add the orange-blossom water and let cool.
instructions.2: Rub the semolina with the ghee until absorbed, add the sugar, coconut and baking powder, then the yogurt and milk, mix until even and rest 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Grease the tray with the tahini, spread half the mixture and level with a wet hand.
instructions.4: Mix the walnuts with the cinnamon and 2 tbsp of syrup; spread the ashta over the base, then the walnuts.
instructions.5: Carefully spread the rest of the mixture over the filling, level it, cut into squares and put a walnut on each.
instructions.6: Bake at 190°C with bottom heat for 30 minutes, then top heat until coloured.
instructions.7: Pour over the cold syrup as soon as it comes out and leave an hour before serving.

add-110.title: Emirati Harees (Wheat and Lamb Porridge)
add-110.culturalNotes: Harees is the dish of celebrations, Ramadan and weddings in the Emirates and the Gulf, traditionally cooked overnight in a pot over embers until the meat melts into the wheat.

instructions.1: Wash the wheat well, soak overnight and drain.
instructions.2: Simmer the meat in the water, skimming, for an hour until it starts to cook.
instructions.3: Add the wheat and salt and cook on very low heat for 3-4 hours, stirring now and then and adding boiling water as it dries, until the meat falls apart and the wheat is fully cooked.
instructions.4: Remove the bones and beat the mixture with the wooden masher (midhrab) or a stick blender until smooth, even and stretchy, adding the cardamom and cinnamon.
instructions.5: Spoon into a dish, make a well in the centre, fill with hot ghee and serve hot.

add-111.title: Turkish Basbousa with Peanuts
add-111.culturalNotes: Turkish basbousa (revani) needs no butter or oil, and the peanuts roasting in the oven give it a special flavour.

add-111-i6.name: Syrup: sugar, water and lemon
add-111-i6.standardAmount: 2 cups sugar + 1½ cups water + a squeeze of lemon

instructions.1: Make the syrup by boiling the sugar, water and lemon for 10 minutes and let it cool.
instructions.2: Mix the semolina, sugar and baking powder, add the milk and fold gently until even without kneading.
instructions.3: Spread in a greased tray and rest 30 minutes, then cut into diamonds and put half a peanut on each.
instructions.4: Bake at 190°C with bottom heat until the edges brown, then top heat for a few minutes until the surface colours.
instructions.5: Pour the cold syrup over while hot and let it soak before serving.

add-112.title: Date Jam (Fresh Red or Ripe Dates)
add-112.culturalNotes: Date jam is a traditional preserve in Egypt and the Gulf. Lemon juice is essential to stop the sugar crystallising in storage.

add-112-i1.name: Red or ripe dates, peeled and pitted

instructions.1: Peel the dates and remove the stones carefully to keep their shape; an almond or clove can go in place of each stone.
instructions.2: Boil the sugar and water until the sugar dissolves, then add the dates and cloves.
instructions.3: Simmer on low heat for 40 minutes without much stirring until the dates turn translucent and the syrup is thick like honey.
instructions.4: Add the lemon five minutes before removing from the heat to stop crystallisation.
instructions.5: Pour hot into sterilised jars and seal.

add-113.title: Crispy Mozzarella Sticks
add-113.culturalNotes: The cheese must be frozen when fried, and frying must be quick and hot, so the crust crisps before the cheese melts and leaks.

add-113-i3.name: Eggs beaten with a spoon of milk

add-113-i4.name: Breadcrumbs with oregano, garlic powder and paprika

add-113-i6.name: Marinara sauce or ketchup to serve

instructions.1: Cut the cheese into sticks 1.5 cm thick and freeze 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Coat in flour, then egg, then seasoned breadcrumbs, then egg and breadcrumbs a second time.
instructions.3: Freeze the coated sticks at least another 30 minutes.
instructions.4: Fry in hot oil at 180°C for only 1-1½ minutes until golden, before the cheese runs.
instructions.5: Drain and serve at once with marinara sauce.

add-114.title: Sawabe' Zeinab (Crispy Fried Fingers in Syrup)
add-114.culturalNotes: Sawabe' Zeinab ('Zeinab's fingers') is an Egyptian Ramadan sweet. The grater pattern isn't just for looks: it adds crunch and helps the syrup seep inside.

add-114-i7.name: Baking powder and a pinch of salt

instructions.1: Mix the flour, semolina, sugar, yeast, baking powder and salt and rub in the oil until absorbed.
instructions.2: Add the yogurt, then the water gradually, and bring into a smooth, firm dough; rest 30 minutes.
instructions.3: Take small pieces and shape into fingers, pressing each on the back of a grater or sieve to take the pattern and rolling it on itself so it is hollow.
instructions.4: Fry in medium oil in batches, turning, until puffed, golden and crisp.
instructions.5: Dip while hot in the cold syrup for a minute, lift out and garnish with pistachios or coconut.

add-115.title: Brined Lupini Beans (Termes)
add-115.culturalNotes: Termes is a popular snack for Sham el-Nessim and festivals in Egypt. The bitterness goes with changing the water, and ready-sweetened lupini need fewer days.

add-115-i4.name: To serve: cumin, lemon and chilli

instructions.1: Wash the lupini and soak in plenty of water for 24 hours.
instructions.2: Boil in fresh water for about an hour until tender but not mushy, then drain.
instructions.3: Soak in cold water, changing it twice a day for 5-7 days until the bitterness is completely gone (taste to check).
instructions.4: Make salted water (1 tbsp salt per litre) and keep the lupini in it in the fridge.
instructions.5: Serve in paper cones or bowls with a pinch of cumin, a squeeze of lemon and chilli.

add-116.title: Dynamite Shrimp
add-116.culturalNotes: Toss the shrimp in the sauce at the last moment so they keep their crunch. Adjust the heat with the amount of sriracha.

add-116-i2.name: Salt, white pepper and garlic powder

add-116-i8.name: For the sauce: sweet chilli sauce

add-116-i9.name: For the sauce: sriracha or chilli sauce

add-116-i10.name: For the sauce: honey and lemon juice

add-116-i11.name: Chopped spring onion and sesame to garnish

instructions.1: Season the shrimp with salt, pepper and garlic, then toss in the egg white.
instructions.2: Mix the cornflour and flour, toss the shrimp in it until fully coated and shake off the excess.
instructions.3: Fry in hot oil in batches for 2-3 minutes until golden and crisp, then drain.
instructions.4: Mix the sauce ingredients in a large bowl until smooth.
instructions.5: Toss the hot shrimp in the sauce just before serving and garnish with spring onion and sesame on lettuce.

add-117.title: Crispy Chinese-Style Coated Nuts
add-117.culturalNotes: The secret is repeating the moisten-and-coat step several times to build the thick crunchy shell. You can deep-fry them instead for a taste closer to the shop-bought kind.

add-117-i4.name: Salted water (1 tsp salt in ½ cup water)

add-117-i6.name: Paprika, garlic powder, curry and chilli

instructions.1: Mix the flour, cornflour and spices in a wide bowl.
instructions.2: Moisten the peanuts with a little of the salted water and soy sauce, toss in the flour mix until coated, and repeat the moistening and coating 3-4 times to build a thick shell.
instructions.3: Sift off the excess flour and toss the nuts with the oil.
instructions.4: Spread on a lined tray and bake at 170°C for 20-25 minutes, stirring every 7 minutes, until golden and crisp.
instructions.5: Let cool completely so they crisp up further, and store in an airtight jar.

add-118.title: Date, Cocoa and Walnut Energy Balls
add-118.culturalNotes: A healthy snack with no added sugar, relying on the natural sweetness of dates. Almonds or cashews can replace the walnuts.

add-118-i6.name: Vanilla and a pinch of salt

instructions.1: If the dates are dry, soak in hot water for 10 minutes and drain well.
instructions.2: Pulse the walnuts and oats coarsely in a food processor, then add the dates, cocoa, peanut butter, vanilla and salt and process until it holds together like dough.
instructions.3: Roll into walnut-sized balls and coat in coconut or cocoa.
instructions.4: Chill 30 minutes until firm and keep in an airtight container in the fridge for two weeks.

add-119.title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Rice Cakes
add-119.culturalNotes: A pinch of flaky salt brings out the chocolate and peanut butter. A quick crunchy snack lighter than biscuits.

add-119-i5.name: Flaky salt or crushed peanuts to garnish

instructions.1: Spread each rice cake with a thin layer of peanut butter and chill 10 minutes.
instructions.2: Melt the chocolate with the coconut oil in the microwave in short bursts until smooth.
instructions.3: Dip the spread side in the chocolate or pour it over and spread with a spoon.
instructions.4: Sprinkle with crushed peanuts or a pinch of flaky salt, chill until the chocolate sets and keep in the fridge.

add-120.title: Puffed Potato Balloons
add-120.culturalNotes: Thin dough and partial drying are the secret of the puff: steam trapped inside the thin piece separates its two surfaces in the hot oil.

instructions.1: Mash the boiled potatoes while hot until completely smooth, add the starch and salt gradually and knead into a smooth, non-sticky dough.
instructions.2: Roll the dough very thin (1-2 mm) between two sheets of baking paper and cut into small squares or circles.
instructions.3: Leave the pieces to air-dry for 2 hours until the surface is dry (or dry in a barely warm oven).
instructions.4: Fry in medium oil, pressing gently with a slotted spoon, until they puff up like balloons and turn golden and crisp.
instructions.5: Drain and sprinkle with salt and paprika while hot.

add-121.title: Yemeni Sahawiq with Cheese
add-121.culturalNotes: Sahawiq is the essential hot relish of the Yemeni table, and adding cheese softens its heat and gives it a creamy texture.

add-121-i5.name: Cheese triangles or soft white cheese

instructions.1: Pound the chillies, garlic and salt in a mortar (mirhak) or chop in a processor.
instructions.2: Add the coriander and pound, then the chopped tomatoes and pound until broken down but still with some texture.
instructions.3: Add the cheese, cumin and lemon and mix until creamy.
instructions.4: Serve at once with rice, mandi and bread.

add-122.title: Egyptian Vermicelli Milk Pudding with Ashta
add-122.culturalNotes: Toasting the vermicelli well in ghee gives this Egyptian pudding its toasty flavour and sets it apart from rice pudding.

add-122-i7.name: Nuts, raisins and coconut to garnish

instructions.1: Toast the vermicelli in the ghee, stirring constantly, until deep golden.
instructions.2: Add the hot milk, sugar and vanilla and simmer 10 minutes until the vermicelli is cooked and slightly thickened.
instructions.3: Pour into a clay dish or oven tray and spread the ashta over the top.
instructions.4: Bake at 200°C for 15 minutes until the top browns.
instructions.5: Garnish with nuts, raisins and coconut and serve hot or cold.

add-123.title: Flaky Chocolate Croissants
add-123.culturalNotes: The secret of flaky croissants is keeping the butter cold and solid between the dough layers, so it turns to steam in the oven and separates them.

add-123-i9.name: Chocolate batons or chopped dark chocolate

instructions.1: Knead everything except the cold butter and chocolate into a smooth dough, wrap and chill an hour.
instructions.2: Roll the cold butter into a thin square between two sheets of baking paper; roll the dough into a rectangle twice its size, place the butter in the middle and enclose it.
instructions.3: Roll the dough into a long rectangle and fold in three like a letter, chill 30 minutes, and repeat the rolling, folding and chilling three times.
instructions.4: Roll the dough 4 mm thick and cut into triangles; place a piece of chocolate at the base of each and roll towards the tip.
instructions.5: Leave an hour until puffed, brush with egg and bake at 200°C for 18-20 minutes until golden.
instructions.6: Quick method: use ready-made puff pastry, cut, fill and bake straight away.

add-124.title: Chicken Caesar Salad
add-124.culturalNotes: Caesar salad was created in Mexico in the 1920s. The lettuce must be completely dry for the creamy dressing to cling to it.

add-124-i4.name: Olive oil and garlic powder for the croutons

add-124-i8.name: For the dressing: lemon juice and mustard

add-124-i9.name: For the dressing: Worcestershire sauce or anchovy fillet (optional)

add-124-i10.name: For the dressing: Parmesan and black pepper

instructions.1: Toss the bread cubes with the olive oil and garlic powder and toast at 190°C for 10 minutes until crisp.
instructions.2: Mix the dressing ingredients until smooth, thinning with a spoon of water if thick.
instructions.3: Tear the lettuce into large pieces after washing and drying it well.
instructions.4: Toss the lettuce with the dressing, add the chicken and croutons, sprinkle with Parmesan and black pepper and serve at once.

add-125.title: Homemade Chocolate Wafers
add-125.culturalNotes: Thin sheets are the secret of the crunch. Keep unfilled sheets in an airtight tin and fill shortly before serving so they don't soften.

add-125-i7.name: For the filling: chocolate spread or thick ganache

instructions.1: Whisk the flour, icing sugar, butter, egg white and vanilla with the water added gradually until a smooth, pourable batter like thin crêpe batter; rest 15 minutes.
instructions.2: Heat a wafer iron or flat non-stick pan, pour a very thin amount of batter and spread it, and cook until dry and pale golden on both sides.
instructions.3: Lift the sheet onto a flat surface to cool and crisp; repeat with the rest.
instructions.4: Beat the chocolate with the soft butter until smooth.
instructions.5: Spread a sheet with filling and top with another, repeating for 3-4 layers, press under a light weight for 5 minutes and cut into rectangles with a sharp knife.

add-126.title: Safflower Lemon Pickle
add-126.culturalNotes: Boiling the lemons briefly speeds up the pickling and removes bitterness from the skin. Safflower gives the golden colour of Egyptian lemon pickle.

instructions.1: Boil the whole lemons for 5-7 minutes until the skin softens slightly, then cool in iced water.
instructions.2: Cut four slits lengthwise in each lemon without separating it at the base.
instructions.3: Mix the safflower, nigella, salt, sugar and chilli and stuff the lemons with it.
instructions.4: Pack the lemons in a sterilised jar with the garlic and chillies, press well and pour over the lemon juice and the rest of the mix.
instructions.5: Cover the top with olive oil, seal and leave in a warm place for 15-20 days, shaking every two days, until the skin softens.

add-127.title: Homemade Pressed Sesame Oil
add-127.culturalNotes: Warm water breaks the oil's bond with the sesame fibres so it separates. The leftover paste can be used like tahini in sweets.

instructions.1: Lightly toast the sesame in a dry pan (optional, for a stronger flavour) and let cool.
instructions.2: Grind the sesame in a powerful grinder or food processor into a smooth paste like tahini.
instructions.3: Add a spoon of warm water and knead and rub the paste hard with a wooden spoon in one direction, then another spoon, until the oil starts to separate from the fibres.
instructions.4: Keep rubbing until the golden oil floats, then tilt the bowl, collect the oil with a spoon and squeeze the paste in cheesecloth to extract the rest.
instructions.5: Let the oil rest an hour so any sediment settles, then strain into a dark bottle and keep in a cool place.

add-128.title: Homemade Creamy Cheese Cups (Gibna Kasat)
add-128.culturalNotes: This soft creamy cheese is like the ready-made Egyptian cup cheese. Processing the curds while warm gives a much smoother texture.

instructions.1: Heat the milk until almost boiling, add the vinegar and stir gently until it separates into curds and whey; leave 5 minutes.
instructions.2: Strain through cheesecloth, keeping a cup of whey, and let the curds drain 15 minutes.
instructions.3: Process the warm curds with the butter, cream, cheese and salt, adding whey a spoon at a time until smooth and creamy.
instructions.4: Pack into cups or jars and chill until set; keeps a week in the fridge.

add-129.title: Alexandrian Hegazeya (Semolina Cinnamon Slice)
add-129.culturalNotes: Hegazeya is a popular Alexandrian sweet, set apart by its semolina and cinnamon filling. The ghee-oil mix gives it crunch with softness.

instructions.1: Rub the semolina and flour with the ghee and oil, add the yeast, sugar and warm water gradually and gather the dough lightly; rest 30 minutes.
instructions.2: Mix the filling ingredients until like wet sand.
instructions.3: Divide the dough in two; press the first half into the base of a greased tray and spread and press the filling on it.
instructions.4: Press the second half over the top, level and cut into squares or diamonds.
instructions.5: Bake at 180°C for 30-35 minutes until the top browns.
instructions.6: Pour the warm syrup over while hot and let cool before serving.

add-130.title: Jameed Sauce for Mansaf
add-130.culturalNotes: Jameed is dried salted yogurt shaped into discs, and the finest comes from Karak. It is the heart of Jordanian mansaf, and stirring in one direction keeps it from splitting.

instructions.1: Break the jameed disc into small pieces and soak in the warm water overnight until soft.
instructions.2: Rub the jameed by hand or blend with its soaking water until completely dissolved, then strain out any grit.
instructions.3: Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly in one direction until it boils, so it doesn't split.
instructions.4: Add the lamb stock gradually with the laban and turmeric and simmer 15 minutes, stirring.
instructions.5: Use the sauce at once to cook the boiled mansaf meat in and pour over the rice, adding no salt since the jameed is salty.

add-131.title: Garlic Lemon Baked Salmon
add-131.culturalNotes: Salmon dries quickly if left too long in the oven. When it flakes in the centre and is still slightly glossy, it is perfectly cooked.

instructions.1: Take the salmon out of the fridge 15 minutes before baking and pat dry.
instructions.2: Mix the butter, garlic, lemon juice, zest and spices.
instructions.3: Place the salmon on a tray lined with baking paper, brush with the mixture and arrange lemon slices around.
instructions.4: Bake at 200°C for just 12-15 minutes until pale pink and flaking easily with a fork.
instructions.5: Spoon over the pan juices and serve with rice or sautéed vegetables.

add-132.title: Duck Soup with Carrots and Potatoes
add-132.culturalNotes: Duck stock is very rich, so skimming the fat once it has cooled a little gives a lighter, clearer soup. Mastic and cardamom soften the duck's strong aroma.

add-132-i6.name: Whole spices: bay leaf, cardamom, mastic, cinnamon stick

instructions.1: Simmer the duck in water to cover with the whole onion and spices, skimming, for 1½ hours until cooked.
instructions.2: Lift out the duck, strain the stock and let it sit a little so the excess fat can be skimmed off.
instructions.3: Sauté the chopped onion in the ghee until soft, add the carrots and potatoes and stir 2 minutes.
instructions.4: Add the strained stock and cook until the vegetables are tender, adding the orzo for the last 10 minutes.
instructions.5: Season and serve the soup hot, and brown the duck in the oven to serve as a main course.

add-133.title: Apricot Jam
add-133.culturalNotes: Apricot jam is one of the quickest jams because apricots are rich in pectin, and skimming the foam gives a clear, glossy jam.

instructions.1: Wash and dry the apricots, open them, remove the stones and cut into pieces as you like.
instructions.2: Put the apricots and sugar in a large pot over medium-high heat and stir until the sugar dissolves and the fruit releases its juice.
instructions.3: When it boils, lower to medium and skim the foam after 10 minutes.
instructions.4: After another 10 minutes add the lemon and cook, stirring, until it reaches the desired thickness.
instructions.5: Pour at once into dry sterilised jars and refrigerate after opening.

add-134.title: Arabic Seven-Spice Blend (Baharat)
add-134.culturalNotes: Seven spice is the base of Levantine cooking for stuffed vegetables, meats and kibbeh. Light toasting before grinding releases the aromatic oils; over-toasting makes it bitter.

instructions.1: Toast the whole spices except the nutmeg in a dry pan over low heat for 2-3 minutes, stirring, until fragrant but not darkened.
instructions.2: Spread on a plate to cool completely.
instructions.3: Grind in a spice grinder to a fine powder and grate the nutmeg over it.
instructions.4: Sift and store in an airtight glass jar away from light; it stays fragrant 3-4 months.

add-135.title: Homemade Garlic and Onion Powder
add-135.culturalNotes: Low heat matters: if it's too high the slices brown and the powder turns bitter. White onions dry better because they contain less sugar.

instructions.1: Slice the garlic thinly and the onions into thin even slices.
instructions.2: Spread the slices on lined trays without overlapping and dry in the oven at 60-70°C with the door slightly open for 3-5 hours, turning every hour, until completely brittle.
instructions.3: Let cool completely, then grind each separately in a spice grinder to a fine powder and sift.
instructions.4: Store each in an airtight jar with a little starch to absorb moisture.
